shots.visual_event: At 11:59 PM, Meera aims a cracked station mirror across the abandoned tracks; the real platform is empty, but the reflection shows Arin’s moving train.
Tick remains quadruped and projects cyan clock marks onto the mirror; his notched ear rotates toward an unheard bell.
A dented brass handbell enters frame. Maya D’Souza, in retired stationmaster uniform and plum shawl, stands behind them.
shots.dialogue_audio: Maya: “No. He hears what the train owes.”

shots.visual_event: Maya unlocks a tiled wall that city maps show as solid; behind it is a sealed arch labelled only with clean editorial text PLATFORM 13.
Maya opens her ledger: faces remain in old photographs, but their names and surrounding memories are blank.
shots.dialogue_audio: Maya: “The train doesn’t hide people. It edits the goodbye.”

shots.visual_event: In the mirror, Arin turns as though he hears Meera. She rings Maya’s bell once; the reflection fractures into thirteen doors.
shots.dialogue_audio: Meera: “Then we make it remember us.”

end_card.text: THE CITY FORGOT AN ENTIRE PLATFORM
